events.factual_description: Birdland Jazz Club presents Meg Okura's Michael Brecker Quindectet Legacy Project featuring Donny McCaslin on October 6, 2026, with sets at 7:00 PM and 9:30 PM. Okura's official project page describes the ensemble as a continuation of Michael Brecker's chamber-jazz Quindectet vision from Wide Angles, developed with the support of Susan Brecker and Darryl Pitt and preserving Gil Goldstein's orchestrations. Okura performed in Brecker's touring Quindectet and was a featured soloist in that repertoire. Her project page states that the October 6 ensemble will include musicians from the original Wide Angles touring ensemble together with additional artists; no additional personnel are named in the primary sources checked here, so none are inferred.

en.why_it_matters: This is not a generic Michael Brecker tribute. Meg Okura played inside Brecker's touring Quindectet and is reviving the unusually detailed chamber-jazz architecture of Wide Angles with permission, archival stewardship and Gil Goldstein's orchestrations still at the center. Putting Donny McCaslin in the tenor chair makes the premise musically alive rather than imitative: one of today's most forceful saxophone voices engaging a Brecker language that helped shape modern large-ensemble jazz, fusion and post-bop. Okura's own Japanese-to-New York trajectory and her orchestral imagination make the project doubly aligned with the Listening Notes thread.
en.trip_verdict: S for New York. Yes, this can justify a dedicated regional trip: the Quindectet repertoire is rarely heard live, Okura has first-hand lineage to the original ensemble, and McCaslin gives the tenor role a strong contemporary identity. It stops short of S+ because this is a legacy revival rather than a singular farewell or one-time historical reunion.

es.why_it_matters: Esto no es un tributo genérico a Michael Brecker. Meg Okura tocó dentro del Quindectet de gira de Brecker y está recuperando la arquitectura de cámara extraordinariamente detallada de Wide Angles con permiso, trabajo de archivo y las orquestaciones de Gil Goldstein todavía en el centro. Poner a Donny McCaslin en la silla de tenor hace que la idea esté musicalmente viva y no sea imitación: una de las voces más fuertes del saxofón actual entrando en un lenguaje de Brecker que ayudó a moldear el jazz de gran ensamble, la fusión y el post-bop modernos. La propia trayectoria Japón–Nueva York de Okura y su imaginación orquestal hacen que el proyecto encaje doblemente con el hilo de Listening Notes.
es.trip_verdict: S para Nueva York. Sí puede justificar un viaje regional dedicado: el repertorio del Quindectet rara vez se escucha en vivo, Okura tiene linaje directo con el ensamble original y McCaslin le da al papel del tenor una identidad contemporánea muy fuerte. No llega a S+ porque es una recuperación de legado, no una despedida singular ni una reunión histórica irrepetible.
